title: Finite inseparable extension making a reduction geometrically reduced
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Assume that $Z$ has finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. There is a finite purely inseparable field extension $k\subseteq k\prime$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] such that $(Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k\prime)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] is geometrically reduced over $k\prime$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]: its base change to every field extension of $k\prime$ is reduced.

proof.text: On every affine chart use [lem-sbc-finite-affine-tensor-base-change] with $r=1$ to identify its field base change with the spectrum of its tensor product. Put $X=Z_{\mathrm{red}}$. On an affine chart with ring $A$, its reduction is $A/N$ for the ideal $N$ of nilpotent elements, and it has the same points as $A$. For every extension $l/k$, the ideal generated by $N$ in $A\otimes_k l$ consists of nilpotent elements: each element is a finite sum of multiples of nilpotents, so a sufficiently large power vanishes. Consequently $(A\otimes_k l)_{\mathrm{red}}=((A/N)\otimes_k l)_{\mathrm{red}}$. The identification sends the class of $a\otimes b$ on each side to the same class. For a localization $S^{-1}B$, a nilpotent fraction $a/s$ has $ta^d=0$ for some $t\in S$ and $d>0$; then $(ta)^d=0$ and $a/s=(ta)/(ts)$ is the image of a fraction with nilpotent numerator. The converse is immediate. Thus $\operatorname{Nil}(S^{-1}B)=S^{-1}\operatorname{Nil}(B)$ and the quotient identifications commute with restriction to standard affine opens. Such opens refine overlaps, so the identifications glue. Reduction is a quotient on affine charts, so $X$ remains locally of finite type and has the same finitely many components as $Z$. It suffices to work with reduced $X$.

source.place: Tag 04KT, proof first paragraph: replace by the reduction

proof.text: List the generic points $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ of $X$ using [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. At $x_i$, choose a finite-type affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$; its corresponding prime $\mathfrak p_i$ is minimal: a strictly smaller prime would give an irreducible closed subset in this chart properly containing the closure of $x_i$, whose closure in $X$ would contradict maximality of its component. The stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] on this chart is $A_{\mathfrak p_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]: the standard neighbourhoods $D(s)$ with $s\notin\mathfrak p_i$ are a neighbourhood basis, their sections are $A_s$, and their germ colimit consists exactly of fractions $a/s$ with the localization equality relation. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field], $K_i=A_{\mathfrak p_i}=\mathcal O_{X,x_i}$ is a field. The kernel of $A\to K_i$ is $\mathfrak p_i$: containment in that prime follows from $sa=0$ with $s\notin\mathfrak p_i$, and the reverse containment follows from $\mathfrak p_iA_{\mathfrak p_i}=0$. Thus $K_i=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p_i)$. The images of finitely many algebra generators of $A$ generate this fraction field as a field over $k$. Every $K_i/k$ is therefore finitely generated.

source.place: Tag 04KT, generic-points paragraph; Algebra Tag 00EU, lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring

proof.text: For any finite purely inseparable extension $l/k$ the projection $X_l\to X$ is a homeomorphism. In positive characteristic $p$, apply [lem-pur-power-generated-spectrum-homeomorphism] on each affine chart to $A\to A\otimes_k l$: its kernel is zero (the vector-space injection $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ has a left inverse induced by a $k$-linear functional on $l$ sending $1$ to $1$), and the generators $1\otimes b$ have a $p$-power in $A$ and $p^r(1\otimes b)=0$ for some $r>0$. In characteristic zero a purely inseparable extension is the identity. Reduction does not change the topology, so $Y_l=(X_l)_{\mathrm{red}}$ has precisely the generic points $x_{i,l}$ over the $x_i$. For $C_i=K_i\otimes_k l$, its reduction is a field. Indeed in characteristic $p$ every $c=\sum_j a_j\otimes b_j$ has $c^{p^r}=\sum_j a_j^{p^r}b_j^{p^r}\in K_i$ for a common $r$; hence a nonzero class in $(C_i)_{\mathrm{red}}$ has nonzero $p^r$-power in $K_i$ and inverse $c^{p^r-1}/c^{p^r}$. The inclusion of $K_i$ is injective by the same vector-space argument. In characteristic zero $C_i=K_i$. Finally $\mathcal O_{Y_l,x_{i,l}}=(C_i)_{\mathrm{red}}$: tensoring the affine chart with $l$ and inverting $A\setminus\mathfrak p_i$ gives $C_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] with $R=A$, $R\prime=A_{\mathfrak p_i}$, $D=A\otimes_k l$; the tensor reassociation sends $(a\otimes b)\otimes(c/s)$ to $(ac/s)\otimes b$; there is exactly one prime over $\mathfrak p_i$ by the homeomorphism. The fraction calculation in step 1 gives $S^{-1}(B/\operatorname{Nil}B)=(S^{-1}B)_{\mathrm{red}}$ for $B=A\otimes_k l$ and $S$ the image of $A\setminus\mathfrak p_i$. The stalk is the further prime localization, by the standard-neighbourhood germ calculation in step 2; further localization does nothing to the field $(C_i)_{\mathrm{red}}$. This supplies the local-ring comparison, rather than merely a topological comparison.

proof.text: Construct a tower $k=k_0\subseteq k_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq k_n$ by induction. Maintain the claim that $k_m/k$ is finite purely inseparable, that $Y_m=(X_{k_m})_{\mathrm{red}}$ has finitely generated generic fields $F_{i,m}$ over $k_m$, and $F_{i,m}\otimes_{k_m}L$ is reduced for every extension $L/k_m$ when $i\le m$. At $m=0$ the field extension is the identity, finite generation is step 2 and the reduced-tensor assertions are empty. At any stage the generic field is the reduction of $K_i\otimes_k k_m$ by step 3. It is a finite extension of $K_i$: the tensor product is finite-dimensional as a $K_i$-vector space and its quotient is a field. It is therefore finitely generated over $k_m$, using the generators of $K_i/k$ and a finite vector-space basis of this extension. For the next stage, step 5 chooses $k_{m+1}/k_m$ finite purely inseparable and step 6 proves that $k_{m+1}/k$ has both properties. Applying step 3 with $l=k_{m+1}$ identifies $F_{i,m+1}$ with $(K_i\otimes_k k_{m+1})_{\mathrm{red}}$; a finite $k$-basis of $k_{m+1}$ spans this quotient over $K_i$, so the same finite-generation conclusion follows from the displayed generators and a basis of that quotient. No quasi-compactness of $X$ is used.

source.place: Tag 04KT, final finite-extension choice, expanded as induction on the finite list

proof.text: Given stage $m<n$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-make-separable] to the finitely generated extension $F_{m+1,m}/k_m$. It gives $k_{m+1}/k_m$ finite purely inseparable and a field $T$ receiving $F_{m+1,m}$ and $k_{m+1}$, with $T/k_{m+1}$ separable. Set $C=F_{m+1,m}\otimes_{k_m}k_{m+1}$. The multiplication map $C\to T$ kills every nilpotent. Conversely its kernel consists of nilpotents: in positive characteristic $c^{p^r}\in F_{m+1,m}$ as in step 3, and if $c$ maps to zero, its power maps to zero in the embedded field $F_{m+1,m}$, hence $c^{p^r}=0$. The characteristic-zero case is the identity. Thus $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ identifies with a subfield $H\subseteq T$ containing $k_{m+1}$, namely the image of $C$. The field is finitely generated over $k_{m+1}$ by step 4. The definition of separability of $T/k_{m+1}$ now implies that this finitely generated subfield $H$ is separably generated over $k_{m+1}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-tensor-reduced] with $K=H$ and $S=L$ for each field extension $L/k_{m+1}$ to obtain the required geometric reducedness of $F_{m+1,m+1}=H$. This proves the tensor-product clause omitted by the statement of the cited 030R node; it is not taken from that node without proof.

proof.text: For $i\le m$, the induction hypothesis says $F_{i,m}\otimes_{k_m}k_{m+1}$ is already reduced. By step 3 it is a field, so it equals the new generic field $F_{i,m+1}$. For any extension $L/k_{m+1}$ the explicit tensor reassociation $(F_{i,m}\otimes_{k_m}k_{m+1})\otimes_{k_{m+1}}L\cong F_{i,m}\otimes_{k_m}L$, $(a\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto a\otimes bc$, with inverse $a\otimes c\mapsto(a\otimes1)\otimes c$, shows that it remains geometrically reduced. Also $((X_{k_m})_{\mathrm{red}}\times_{k_m}k_{m+1})_{\mathrm{red}}=(X_{k_{m+1}})_{\mathrm{red}}$ by the nilpotent-ideal computation in step 1. Thus this induction actually concerns the asserted reduced base changes. Finiteness and pure inseparability of $k_{m+1}/k$ follow by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-transitive].

proof.text: At $m=n$, the reduced scheme $Y_n$ has all its generic local rings geometrically reduced by the induction. Apply [lem-pur-geometric-reducedness-from-generic-stalks] to $Y_n$ over $k_n$. It is geometrically reduced over $k_n$, and $k_n/k$ is finite purely inseparable. Step 1 identifies $Y_n$ with $(Z_{k_n})_{\mathrm{red}}$, giving the conclusion. If $X$ is empty, $n=0$, choose $k_n=k$; the criterion has vacuous generic-point hypotheses and gives the same conclusion.
